# React buildout rules (plugin) — run ONCE during repo creation, then discarded.
# One-time structural checks that the linter enforces React's Rules of Hooks, and
# that the feature-import boundaries are enforced at both scopes they span — the
# in-project linter rule and the cross-project module-boundary tag rule; the
# ongoing React code judgment (cross-feature imports,
# server-state-in-global-store, unsanitized HTML) lives in
# shapes/react.llmlint.yml, and the shared web-app buildout rule covers the
# generic production-build case.
version: 2.0.0

rules:
  - name: react_hooks_lint_rules_enabled
    description: |
      true when the lint config enables the Rules of Hooks and the effect
      dependency check — `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` with `rules-of-hooks` and
      `exhaustive-deps` as errors, or the Biome equivalents (`useHookAtTopLevel`,
      `useExhaustiveDependencies`). false when neither is configured, so hook
      misuse and stale-closure effect bugs pass the gate.
    files:
      include:
        - "**/eslint.config.*"
        - "**/.eslintrc*"
        - "**/biome.json"
        - "**/biome.jsonc"
        - "**/package.json"
    relevance: the target files configure the JS/TS linter

  - name: feature_import_boundaries_enforced_at_both_scopes
    description: |
      true when the unidirectional feature-import architecture is enforced at both
      scopes it spans: inside an app project by the linter — an
      `import/no-restricted-paths` (ESLint) or `noRestrictedImports` (Biome) rule
      banning cross-feature internal imports and shared code importing from
      features — and between projects by the orchestrator's module-boundary tag
      rule, so a second app cannot reach into the first's `src/` instead of
      depending on a shared UI project. false when either scope is unenforced,
      leaving the shared → features → app boundary to convention where it is
      easiest to cross.
    files:
      include:
        - "**/eslint.config.*"
        - "**/.eslintrc*"
        - "**/biome.json"
        - "**/biome.jsonc"
        - "nx.json"
        - "**/project.json"
    relevance: the target files configure the JS/TS linter's import rules or the project boundary tags
